source.stem: Which of the following statements about the scope and definition of the biosphere is correct: () A. The general name of all living things on the earth; B. All of the atmosphere, hydrosphere and lithosphere; C. The place where all living things on the earth can live; D. All living things on the earth and the environment in which they live

hinge.title: Decide whether an observed place is a habitat by checking whether an organism lives there and whether the place provides living and non-living conditions for life.
node_labels: Living systems: organisms, health and ecosystems

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: habitat is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: A place can be a habitat even if it is small, such as a large tree, when organisms live there.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when A place can be a habitat even if it is small, such as a large tree, when organisms live there is not true.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Judge from the most visible feature in the figure, not from the mechanism's test.

intelligence.enrichment: A habitat is the place where an organism lives; every habitat includes living beings and non-living physical conditions such as air, sunlight, water, temperature, and soil. Habitat conditions and available resources shape which organisms can live there and how they use those resources. The learner correctly applies this rule: A habitat is the place where an organism lives; every habitat includes living beings and non-living physical conditions such as air, sunlight, water, temperature, and soil. A habitat means only a large natural place like a pond or forest, so the bark of a tree cannot be a habitat.
